solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Crew member's company detains sailor in Boar's Head

indicators.note: to detain is to hold someone in custody, so the company holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: Coy. is the military abbreviation for company

indicators.note: the head of anything is its top, so the head of Boar is its first letter

explanation.surface: A sailor is kept drinking at the Boar’s Head, a pub, by his shipmates.
explanation.walkthrough: Coy. for company is an army abbreviation rarely seen outside military lists, so the usual CO misleads here. The Boar’s Head reads as a pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain description: a cabin boy is the youngest hand on a ship, waiting on officers, so a member of its crew.

clue.text: Commander, completely upset, initially resisted arrest

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for Commanding Officer, a commander

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: all, as in all over, completely

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of resisted

explanation.surface: A police report: the commanding officer was thoroughly upset when the suspect at first resisted arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns a word upside down, i.e. reads it backwards; 'arrest' is a verb here, the police sense of seizing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To collar someone is the informal police verb for seizing or apprehending them.

clue.text: Singer is mafia grass according to Spooner

indicators.note: according to Spooner tells us to swap the opening sounds of the two words, after the Rev. William Spooner

parts.note: a mob is an organised crime gang such as the Mafia
barley is a cereal grass, its name said 'bar-lee'

explanation.surface: A singer is accused of being a mafia informer, in the Rev. Spooner's version of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' tempts as informer, fitting the mafia story, but here it is the cereal plant. 'according to Spooner' swaps the M and B of MOB BARLEY to give the reggae singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Marley was the Jamaican reggae star who sang No Woman, No Cry, i.e. a famous vocalist.

clue.text: Dancer's series returning — watch on 5

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so the series runs backwards
in a down clue, one thing on another sits above it, so the watch goes on top of the 5

explanation.surface: A dancer’s television series comes back, to be watched on channel 5.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' looks like a TV channel, but it is just the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Rudolf Nureyev was the most famous ballet dancer of his era.

clue.text: Nothing soppy about beginning to like little bird

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, means nothing

indicators.note: about tells us the word for soppy goes round the letter that follows

parts.note: wet, in British slang, means soppy or feeble

indicators.note: beginning to picks out the first letter of like

explanation.surface: A sentimental onlooker is starting to warm to a tiny bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps WET round L, the first letter of like ('beginning to'), giving WLET, and O for nothing comes first. 'Wet' is British slang for a feeble or sentimental person.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a young or small owl, so it is a small bird.

clue.text: Infatuation with books about language

parts.note: pash = a schoolgirl crush, British slang

indicators.note: to turn about is to face the other way, so the books are reversed

explanation.surface: Someone has a crush on books about language.
explanation.walkthrough: A pash is dated British slang for a crush.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this is the tongue of the Pashtun people of Afghanistan and Pakistan, one language among many.

clue.text: Beer guzzling job for true believer

indicators.note: to guzzle is to swallow greedily, so the beer swallows the job whole

explanation.surface: Drinking beer is a job for a real enthusiast.
explanation.walkthrough: Beyond the twelve disciples, the word is used of any passionate advocate of a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: An extended sense: the first followers sent out by Jesus give a name to any fervent believer or champion.

clue.text: Run in stockings for Jade, perhaps

indicators.note: one thing in another is inside it, so the run sits within the stockings

parts.note: R = run, as in cricket scores

explanation.surface: A woman called Jade has a ladder in her stockings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' is a ladder in tights, and Jade looks like a woman’s name; a jade is an old, worn-out nag.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by 'perhaps': a jade is a tired or worthless specimen of the animal.

clue.text: Extrovert in latter stages of incumbency?

definitions.meaning: an extrovert is sociable and friendly
said of an office-holder about to leave the post

explanation.surface: A sociable office-holder nears the end of their term.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are adjectives; the second is the one used of a president or chairman about to step down.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: friendly and sociable, and departing from office, as in the outgoing government.

clue.text: Succeed, for example, after experiencing setback? Thanks, boss

indicators.note: experiencing setback means the letters for 'for example' are set back, i.e. reversed

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example
ta is British informal for thanks
the head is the boss or person in charge

explanation.surface: Someone who suffers a setback but still thanks the boss on the way to success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' sounds like a misfortune in the surface, but it tells us to set the abbreviation back to front. Ta is British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: To get ahead is an idiom for making progress and prospering, especially in a career.

clue.text: After abundant protest, whip accepts Republican Party member

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the whip takes the Republican inside
after means following, so the whip comes after abundant protest

parts.note: a liberal helping = an abundant one

explanation.surface: After a big protest, a party whip lets a Republican join.
explanation.walkthrough: Whip and party read as parliamentary jargon; the whip is a lash. The Liberal Democrats are a British political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a Lib Dem belongs to one of Britain’s main political parties.

clue.text: Register reportedly concludes article by American pundit

indicators.note: by means placed beside, so the abbreviation for American sits next to the article
concludes says the sounded-out word comes at the end, after the other pieces
reportedly means as heard, so we write a word that sounds like the one meant

parts.note: a register is a list, a word that sounds like 'lyst'

explanation.surface: A newspaper register rounds off a piece by a US commentator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' means the word for Register is written as it sounds, not as it is spelt; 'by' sets the American abbreviation beside the article and 'concludes' puts the sounded word last.
explanation.definitionFit: A pundit is an expert commentator, and an analyst is someone who examines and comments on events.

clue.text: Firm following free trade style

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the firm goes after the rearranged letters
freed letters are no longer tied to their order, so trade is rearranged

explanation.surface: A company adopts a free-trade way of doing business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free trade' looks like economics; 'free' is only there to rearrange the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the geometric design look of the 1920s and 30s is one artistic style.

clue.text: Bone's depleted cell area left in clamp

indicators.note: one thing in another is inside it, so left goes within the clamp
something depleted has been emptied, so cell loses its middle and keeps its outside

parts.note: CELL emptied of its middle letters
a vice is a clamping tool

explanation.surface: A bone lies in a shrunken prison cell, held in a clamp.
explanation.walkthrough: Vice is the British spelling of the clamp Americans call a vise.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the collarbone is one bone of the skeleton.

clue.text: Stupid advice to overworked setter?

definitions.meaning: an overworked setter should write fewer clues; split the answer 4 + 4

explanation.surface: Someone gives a stupid piece of advice to a tired crossword setter.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic: split the answer as CLUE LESS, an instruction to a setter with too many clues to write.
explanation.definitionFit: Two readings: an informal synonym for stupid, and literally 'write fewer clues', the advice.

clue.text: The Spanish film's last caption's mischievous

parts.note: FIN, 'the end', closes many old films

explanation.surface: A Spanish film ends with a playful caption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' tempts you to take a final letter, but the whole French word for 'end' is the film's last caption.
explanation.definitionFit: An extended sense: like an elf, so impish and playfully mischievous.

clue.text: Onset of frost threatened to overwhelm British garden feature

indicators.note: the onset of something is its start, so take the first letter of frost
to overwhelm is to engulf

parts.note: to lower (rhymes with flower) = to scowl, look threatening

explanation.surface: The first frost threatens to ruin a British garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Lower here is the verb pronounced like 'flower', meaning to frown or look menacing, as a dark sky does.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a planted plot is one feature a garden may have.

clue.text: Spoiled international politician given publicity

explanation.surface: A spoilt international politician gets media attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoiled' reads as pampered but means damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of damaged: something spoiled has been weakened or harmed.

clue.text: Perhaps millions live on for ever

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another is added after it, so live follows for ever

explanation.surface: Perhaps millions of people will live for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: Aye for always is poetic and Scottish, and may be spelt with or without the E.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are adverbs of possibility that swap freely in 'X it will rain'.

clue.text: Composed more war music that drives people crazy

indicators.note: to compose is to put together, so the letters are assembled anew

explanation.surface: A composer writes more war music, a tune that maddens listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' fits the music surface perfectly, which hides its job of rearranging the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a catchy tune stuck in the head, playing over and over until it maddens you.

clue.text: Fewer than 500 try backing unlikely winner

indicators.note: backing is moving backwards, so the try is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Fewer than 500 people bet on the outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' reads as betting, which suits an outsider; it means reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the competitor expected to lose would be an unlikely one to win.

clue.text: Observe others keeping quiet on city

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the others hold the rest inside
in a down clue, one thing on another sits above it, so quiet goes on top of city

parts.note: EC = the City of London postcode

explanation.surface: Watch the others staying quiet about the city.
explanation.walkthrough: The City, the financial district of London, has the postcode EC. 'Observe' is not watching but obeying.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of abiding by: to observe a law or custom is to honour it.

clue.text: Caught somebody without European pass

indicators.note: without means lacking, so somebody goes without its European letter

explanation.surface: Someone was caught without a valid European travel pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' looks like a document, but it is a way through mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: a pass is a route through mountains, and a deep gorge can serve as one.

clue.text: Trim line on archbishop's cloak and dress

indicators.note: on means the trimming and line are placed after the archbishop's outer letters
a cloak is the outer covering, so the archbishop is reduced to its outside letters

parts.note: the word archbishop; its possessive ties it to the cloak
to pare is to trim by cutting away the edges

explanation.surface: A tailor trims a line of braid on a bishop's vestment and robe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cloak' tempts as a garment, since this is a church outfit, but it means only the outside letters of archbishop survive; 'on' in an across clue puts the trimming and line after them.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is clothing in general; dress, as a mass noun, means the same thing.

clue.text: Writing introduction to perennial beauty

indicators.note: an introduction comes first, so take the first letter of perennial

parts.note: a rose, as a beauty among flowers

explanation.surface: An essay introduces a beautiful perennial plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Perennial and beauty both sound like gardening, which fits the flower neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: ordinary, non-verse language is one kind of writing.

clue.text: Part of mosaic seen in square's setting from the east

indicators.note: something seen in a place is visible inside it, so the letters sit within the words
in an across clue, east is the right-hand end, so read from right to left

explanation.surface: A mosaic tile appears in a square’s pattern, viewed from the east side.
explanation.walkthrough: Mosaic, square and setting all belong together, which helps hide the backwards letters across the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A precise term: the small cube of stone or glass set into a mosaic, one part of the whole.

clue.text: Bizet ultimately snubbed award for opera

indicators.note: ultimately picks out the final letter of Bizet
snubbed, like a snub nose, means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an Oscar is the film industry's award

explanation.surface: The composer of Carmen is finally passed over for an award for his opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bizet ultimately' gives T, and 'snubbed award' cuts OSCAR to OSCA. Bizet wrote Carmen, so 'opera' seems to be his; the answer is Puccini's.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca is Puccini's 1900 opera about a singer, a painter and a police chief in Rome.

clue.text: Absolutism rose disastrously before conclusion of bloody disorder

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in chaos, so the letters are thrown into a new order
the conclusion is the end, so take the last letter of bloody

explanation.surface: Absolute rule rose disastrously before ending in bloody disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: The Y joins the anagram fodder. The answer is also an old British legal term for a violent gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a violent, unruly gathering is one form of public disorder.

clue.text: Simply gorgeous model my dear

indicators.note: to model clay is to shape it, so the letters are shaped into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone gushes to a model, calling her simply gorgeous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' reads as a person being flattered; it is the verb, shaping the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: something so lovely it seems out of a dream is simply gorgeous.

clue.text: Love in staff party ending in conviction for old beast

indicators.note: one thing in another is inside it, so love sits within staff party

parts.note: a mast is a pole, a staff

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: An office romance at the staff party ends in a conviction for an old brute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff party' looks like one office event, but staff is a pole and the love goes between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the extinct elephant-like animal is one ancient beast.
